  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

While coverage runs, let me study the two functions to plan the refactor and look at the existing tests to know what's covered. Let me review test_configLoader.js and test_buildEncodedConfig.js to understand the test framework patterns and current coverage of branches.

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

While coverage runs, let me study the two functions to plan the refactor and look at the existing tests to know what's covered. Let me review test_configLoader.js and test_buildEncodedConfig.js to understand the test framework patterns and current coverage of branches.

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

While coverage runs, let me study the two functions to plan the refactor and look at the existing tests to know what's covered. Let me review test_configLoader.js and test_buildEncodedConfig.js to understand the test framework patterns and current coverage of branches.

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

While coverage runs, let me study the two functions to plan the refactor and look at the existing tests to know what's covered. Let me review test_configLoader.js and test_buildEncodedConfig.js to understand the test framework patterns and current coverage of branches.

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

While coverage runs, let me study the two functions to plan the refactor and look at the existing tests to know what's covered. Let me review test_configLoader.js and test_buildEncodedConfig.js to understand the test framework patterns and current coverage of branches.

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

While coverage runs, let me study the two functions to plan the refactor and look at the existing tests to know what's covered. Let me review test_configLoader.js and test_buildEncodedConfig.js to understand the test framework patterns and current coverage of branches.

The main complexity drivers:

**loadProjectConfig**: many sequential if-blocks. CC ~high. Extract helpers:
- `decideConfigSource(params, customParams)` → returns {loaded, resolvedPath} — loop over candidate sources (configPath, customParams.configPath, agentConfigsDir path, '.dmtools/config.js', '../.dmtools/config.js'). Careful: log lines must be the same. We can build candidates array and loop.
- `applyRepositoryOverrides(config, params, customParams)` — repository, targetRepository.
- `applyBranchResolver(config, params, key, candidatePath...)` — baseBranch/snapshotBranch resolvers share structure; extract a helper `applyBranchResolverFn(config, params, pathKey, assignFn, candidateFn, label)`. But careful about log lines.
- `applyCustomParamHooks(config, customParams)` — branchNamingFnPath, prSearchFnPath.
- `applySimpleCustomParamSwitches(config, customParams)` — featureBranchEnabled, scmProvider.

**buildEncodedConfig**: complex. Extract:
- `copyParamValue(p, key, value, effectiveConfig)` — the skipKeys + type dispatch.
- `applyResolvedInstructions(p, resolved)` — the big if-block.
- metadata building.

Goal CRAP < 30 for both functions. CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage; with coverage it's less. Actually formula: CRAP = CC²·(1-cov)³ + CC. With tests covering many branches, existing CRAP is 54.2 and 57 presumably at current coverage. Hmm, ticket says loadProjectConfig 54.2, buildEncodedConfig 57 — these are current measured values with coverage. So we need to bring below 30 via combination of coverage increase + CC reduction.

Let me compute: if CC stays same and we raise coverage... CRAP = CC²(1-cov)³ + CC. For loadProjectConfig, CRAP 54.2: if CC=8, then 64(1-cov)³+8 = 54.2 → (1-cov)³ = 0.72 → cov ≈ 0.107. Hmm. For buildEncodedConfig 57: if CC=9, 81(1-cov)³+9=57 → (1-cov)³≈0.59, cov≈0.18.

To get under 30: e.g. CC=8 needs 64(1-cov)³+8 < 30 → (1-cov)³ < 0.34 → cov > 30%. And reducing CC helps quadratically. New functions must be ≤8 CRAP (or covered). Threshold 8 for new functions — meaning a new function with CC 2 uncovered is fine (4+2=6≤8), CC 3 uncovered = 12 > 8 — so cover new helpers.

Strategy: extract helpers AND add characterization tests covering branches of both the main functions and helpers. The instruction: "extract pure helpers (parse*/build*/decide*) and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

messages.preview: Found it — my generic hook helper assigned `branchNamingFn` to `config` instead of `config.git`. Fix:

blocks.text:
The test 'loads function from branchNamingFnPath' serves fnFileContent — for this test the fn file content is the `fnSrc` string. Wait — "expected function but got object" — the module loaded but exports wasn't a function. The fnSrc in the test: `'module.exports = function(ticket, branchRole) {...}'`. loadConfigFile evals via `new Function('module','exports','require', content)`.

Hmm — but original loadProjectConfig ALSO used loadConfigFile for branchNamingFnPath... identical. Why does it fail NOW? What changed? loadCustomParamFnHook: `var path = customParams[key];` — `path`!! I named a variable `path` — shadowing... no, in GralJS/node there's no global path conflict in this eval context... The module evals inside a function wrapper; `var path` is local. Hmm.

Wait — actually look: in loadConfigFile, `var content = tryReadFile(path)` — parameter named path ✓ fine.

The REAL issue may be variable name collision in my helper `loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, key, exportKey)`: no.

Let me look at the failing test more closely — 'branchNamingFnPath takes priority': got "object" for typeof config.git.branchNamingFn. So loadConfigFile returned an object (module.exports={}?). That happens when `content` is... if tryReadFile returned null → loadConfigFile returns null → typeof null !== 'function' → warn path (we see the warn in test 3's output). For tests 1-2, no warn shown, and 'Loaded branchNamingFn from js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js' printed — so fn WAS truthy and typeof=='function' passed?? But then config.git.branchNamingFn = fn. Yet test sees object.

OH WAIT. I see it! `loadCustomParamFnHook` parameter name `path`... In `new Function('module','exports','require', content)` no. Hmm but the test's fakeFileRead: `return reads[p] || null;` fine.

Actually — think about `var fn = loadConfigFile(path);` — `path` here is customParams.branchNamingFnPath = 'js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js'. loadConfigFile calls tryReadFile(path) → file_read({path: path}) → fnSrc string → new Function eval → moduleObj.exports = function ✓ typeof 'function' ✓ config.branchNamingFn = fn... then test asserts typeof config.git.branchNamingFn === 'function' but got 'object'.

UNLESS loadProjectConfig's later steps OVERWRITE config.git.branchNamingFn. What runs after loadCustomParamFnHook? applyCustomParamOverrides — doesn't touch branchNamingFn. Hmm.

OR: config.git.branchNamingFn gets lost in mergeProjectConfig — merge happens before. No.

Wait — maybe the problem is `config[exportKey] = fn;` where exportKey = 'branchNamingFn' → sets config.branchNamingFn, NOT config.git.branchNamingFn!!! THE BUG. Original code: `config.git.branchNamingFn = namingFn;`. My generic helper sets config[exportKey] = top-level config.branchNamingFn! And for prSearchFn: original `config.prSearchFn = prSearchFn;` — top-level ✓. So branchNamingFn must go under config.git.

Fix: pass a target object or setter. Change helper to take (config, customParams, key, targetKey) where targetKey is e.g. 'git.branchNamingFn' path... Simpler: give the helper the assignment target object: loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams, 'branchNamingFnPath', 'branchNamingFn') and loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, 'prSearchFnPath', 'prSearchFn'). But then the log message uses exportKey — same strings ✓.

But wait — test 3 ('warns and ignores when file does not export function') expects config.git.branchNamingFn to stay unset and warn mentions 'branchNamingFnPath' — with target=config.git and key='branchNamingFnPath' ✓ same.
Found it — my generic hook helper assigned `branchNamingFn` to `config` instead of `config.git`. Fix:

 * ticket without mutating the original params/jobParams objects.
 *
 * @param {Object} params - Full action params (may have .jobParams and/or .ticket)

 */

    var ticket = (base && base.ticket) || (params && params.ticket);
    if (ticket && base.ticket !== ticket) {

    }
    return base;
}

blocks.text:
The test 'loads function from branchNamingFnPath' serves fnFileContent — for this test the fn file content is the `fnSrc` string. Wait — "expected function but got object" — the module loaded but exports wasn't a function. Hmm — but original loadProjectConfig ALSO used loadConfigFile for branchNamingFnPath... identical. Why does it fail NOW? What changed? loadCustomParamFnHook: `var path = customParams[key];` — `path`!! I named a variable `path` — shadowing... no, in GralJS/node there's no global path conflict in this eval context... The module evals inside a function wrapper; `var path` is local. Hmm.

Wait — actually look: in loadConfigFile, `var content = tryReadFile(path)` — parameter named path ✓ fine.

The REAL issue may be variable name collision in my helper `loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, key, exportKey)`: no.

Let me look at the failing test more closely — 'branchNamingFnPath takes priority': got "object" for typeof config.git.branchNamingFn. So loadConfigFile returned an object (module.exports={}?). That happens when `content` is... if tryReadFile returned null → loadConfigFile returns null → typeof null !== 'function' → warn path (we see the warn in test 3's output). For tests 1-2, no warn shown, and 'Loaded branchNamingFn from js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js' printed — so fn WAS truthy and typeof=='function' passed?? But then config.git.branchNamingFn = fn. Yet test sees object.

OH WAIT. I see it! `loadCustomParamFnHook` parameter name `path`... In `new Function('module','exports','require', content)` no. Hmm but the test's fakeFileRead: `return reads[p] || null;` fine.

Actually — think about `var fn = loadConfigFile(path);` — `path` here is customParams.branchNamingFnPath = 'js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js'. loadConfigFile calls tryReadFile(path) → file_read({path: path}) → fnSrc string → new Function eval → moduleObj.exports = function ✓ typeof 'function' ✓ config.branchNamingFn = fn... then test asserts typeof config.git.branchNamingFn === 'function' but got 'object'.

UNLESS loadProjectConfig's later steps OVERWRITE config.git.branchNamingFn. What runs after loadCustomParamFnHook? applyCustomParamOverrides — doesn't touch branchNamingFn. Hmm.

OR: config.git.branchNamingFn gets lost in mergeProjectConfig — merge happens before. No.

Wait — maybe the problem is `config[exportKey] = fn;` where exportKey = 'branchNamingFn' → sets config.branchNamingFn, NOT config.git.branchNamingFn!!! THE BUG. Original code: `config.git.branchNamingFn = namingFn;`. My generic helper sets config[exportKey] = top-level config.branchNamingFn! And for prSearchFn: original `config.prSearchFn = prSearchFn;` — top-level ✓. So branchNamingFn must go under config.git.

Fix: pass a target object or setter. Change helper to take (config, customParams, key, targetKey) where targetKey is e.g. 'git.branchNamingFn' path... Simpler: give the helper the assignment target object: loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams, 'branchNamingFnPath', 'branchNamingFn') and loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, 'prSearchFnPath', 'prSearchFn'). But then the log message uses exportKey — same strings ✓.

But wait — test 3 ('warns and ignores when file does not export function') expects config.git.branchNamingFn to stay unset and warn mentions 'branchNamingFnPath' — with target=config.git and key='branchNamingFnPath' ✓ same.
Found it — my generic hook helper assigned `branchNamingFn` to `config` instead of `config.git`. Fix:

blocks.text:
The test 'loads function from branchNamingFnPath' serves fnFileContent — for this test the fn file content is the `fnSrc` string. Hmm — but original loadProjectConfig ALSO used loadConfigFile for branchNamingFnPath... identical. Why does it fail NOW? What changed? loadCustomParamFnHook: `var path = customParams[key];` — `path`!! I named a variable `path` — shadowing... no, in GralJS/node there's no global path conflict in this eval context... The module evals inside a function wrapper; `var path` is local. Hmm.

Wait — actually look: in loadConfigFile, `var content = tryReadFile(path)` — parameter named path ✓ fine.

The REAL issue may be variable name collision in my helper `loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, key, exportKey)`: no.

Let me look at the failing test more closely — 'branchNamingFnPath takes priority': got "object" for typeof config.git.branchNamingFn. So loadConfigFile returned an object (module.exports={}?). That happens when `content` is... if tryReadFile returned null → loadConfigFile returns null → typeof null !== 'function' → warn path (we see the warn in test 3's output). For tests 1-2, no warn shown, and 'Loaded branchNamingFn from js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js' printed — so fn WAS truthy and typeof=='function' passed?? But then config.git.branchNamingFn = fn. Yet test sees object.

OH WAIT. I see it! `loadCustomParamFnHook` parameter name `path`... In `new Function('module','exports','require', content)` no. Hmm but the test's fakeFileRead: `return reads[p] || null;` fine.

Actually — think about `var fn = loadConfigFile(path);` — `path` here is customParams.branchNamingFnPath = 'js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js'. loadConfigFile calls tryReadFile(path) → file_read({path: path}) → fnSrc string → new Function eval → moduleObj.exports = function ✓ typeof 'function' ✓ config.branchNamingFn = fn... then test asserts typeof config.git.branchNamingFn === 'function' but got 'object'.

UNLESS loadProjectConfig's later steps OVERWRITE config.git.branchNamingFn. What runs after loadCustomParamFnHook? applyCustomParamOverrides — doesn't touch branchNamingFn. Hmm.

OR: config.git.branchNamingFn gets lost in mergeProjectConfig — merge happens before. No.

Wait — maybe the problem is `config[exportKey] = fn;` where exportKey = 'branchNamingFn' → sets config.branchNamingFn, NOT config.git.branchNamingFn!!! THE BUG. Original code: `config.git.branchNamingFn = namingFn;`. My generic helper sets config[exportKey] = top-level config.branchNamingFn! And for prSearchFn: original `config.prSearchFn = prSearchFn;` — top-level ✓. So branchNamingFn must go under config.git.

Fix: pass a target object or setter. Change helper to take (config, customParams, key, targetKey) where targetKey is e.g. 'git.branchNamingFn' path... Simpler: give the helper the assignment target object: loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams, 'branchNamingFnPath', 'branchNamingFn') and loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, 'prSearchFnPath', 'prSearchFn'). But then the log message uses exportKey — same strings ✓.

But wait — test 3 ('warns and ignores when file does not export function') expects config.git.branchNamingFn to stay unset and warn mentions 'branchNamingFnPath' — with target=config.git and key='branchNamingFnPath' ✓ same.

blocks.text:
The test 'loads function from branchNamingFnPath' serves fnFileContent — for this test the fn file content is the `fnSrc` string. The module evals inside a function wrapper; `var path` is local. Hmm.

Wait — actually look: in loadConfigFile, `var content = tryReadFile(path)` — parameter named path ✓ fine.

The REAL issue may be variable name collision in my helper `loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, key, exportKey)`: no.

Let me look at the failing test more closely — 'branchNamingFnPath takes priority': got "object" for typeof config.git.branchNamingFn. So loadConfigFile returned an object (module.exports={}?). For tests 1-2, no warn shown, and 'Loaded branchNamingFn from js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js' printed — so fn WAS truthy and typeof=='function' passed?? But then config.git.branchNamingFn = fn. Yet test sees object.

OH WAIT. I see it! `loadCustomParamFnHook` parameter name `path`... In `new Function('module','exports','require', content)` no. Hmm but the test's fakeFileRead: `return reads[p] || null;` fine.

Actually — think about `var fn = loadConfigFile(path);` — `path` here is customParams.branchNamingFnPath = 'js/branchNaming/issueType_naming.js'. loadConfigFile calls tryReadFile(path) → file_read({path: path}) → fnSrc string → new Function eval → moduleObj.exports = function ✓ typeof 'function' ✓ config.branchNamingFn = fn... then test asserts typeof config.git.branchNamingFn === 'function' but got 'object'.

UNLESS loadProjectConfig's later steps OVERWRITE config.git.branchNamingFn. What runs after loadCustomParamFnHook? applyCustomParamOverrides — doesn't touch branchNamingFn. Hmm.

OR: config.git.branchNamingFn gets lost in mergeProjectConfig — merge happens before. No.

Wait — maybe the problem is `config[exportKey] = fn;` where exportKey = 'branchNamingFn' → sets config.branchNamingFn, NOT config.git.branchNamingFn!!! THE BUG. Original code: `config.git.branchNamingFn = namingFn;`. My generic helper sets config[exportKey] = top-level config.branchNamingFn! Fix: pass a target object or setter. Change helper to take (config, customParams, key, targetKey) where targetKey is e.g. 'git.branchNamingFn' path... Simpler: give the helper the assignment target object: loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams, 'branchNamingFnPath', 'branchNamingFn') and loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams, 'prSearchFnPath', 'prSearchFn'). But then the log message uses exportKey — same strings ✓.

But wait — test 3 ('warns and ignores when file does not export function') expects config.git.branchNamingFn to stay unset and warn mentions 'branchNamingFnPath' — with target=config.git and key='branchNamingFnPath' ✓ same.
Found it — my generic hook helper assigned `branchNamingFn` to `config` instead of `config.git`. Fix:

Done. Summary of the gh-1039 CRAP reduction:

## Results

| Function | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `configLoader.loadProjectConfig` | CRAP 54.2 (CC 53) | **CRAP 4.0 (CC 4)** |

Every other function's CRAP is unchanged; coverage of both target functions is 100%.

## What was done

1. **Characterization tests first (TDD)** — 17 new tests pinning previously uncovered behavior (`params.repository`, agentConfigsDir convention, throwing/falsy/unreadable branch resolvers, partial `targetRepository`, `scmProvider`, parent-merge depth guard, missing parents, non-array merges, metadata derivation). Two initially "obvious" test expectations were wrong and were corrected to pin *actual* behavior (child params override parent in merges; a `config.js` basename contributes no project key).

2. **Pure helper extraction** — discovery probe loop (`buildConfigCandidates`/`discoverProjectConfig`), repository overrides, shared base/snapshot branch resolver (`runBranchResolver`/`resolveCandidateBranch`), shared `*FnPath` hook loader, and on the builder side `resolveProjectKey`, `resolveAgentJsonPath`, `copyParamValue`/`copyAgentParams`, `applyInstructionExtras`/`applyCliPrompts`/`applyConfigPatches`, `resolveFieldNameOverride`, `buildMetadata`. Log lines, warn messages, call order, and patch ordering are byte-identical; one real regression was caught by the characterization tests (`branchNamingFn` must land on `config.git`, not `config`) and fixed.

3. **Verification** — canonical runner `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`: **4279 passed, 0 failed**; node coverage harness green; local `crap4js` measurement (same pipeline as CI) confirms targets well under 30 and all new functions ≤ 8.
